summary: This skill guides an agent through migrating a nansen-cli wallet password from a ~/.nansen/.env file or a .credentials file into the OS keychain. It does this with the `nansen` CLI (`wallet secure`, `wallet export --reveal`, `forget-password`, `auth status`, `doctor`), and it installs the npm package nansen-cli. It handles the wallet password (NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD) and decrypts the wallet's private keys for verification, with output discarded. It also relies on NANSEN_API_KEY or a browser session. requires.env declares nothing, and the files name no outbound host other than a github.com documentation link.

findings.message: NANSEN_API_KEY is set as primaryEnv, and line 45 says it takes precedence, yet metadata.openclaw.requires declares only the nansen binary and no env vars.
The workflow depends on the NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD environment variable (also lines 112, 172, 194), which is a wallet-decrypting secret that requires.env does not declare.
Step 1 has the agent ask the human for the wallet password, or read it from ~/.nansen/.env if authorized, so the agent handles a credential that decrypts the wallet's private keys.

The `source ~/.nansen/.env && nansen wallet secure` command executes the env file as shell code and exports the wallet password into the process, and the skill-card's own mitigation (line 58) warns against sourcing credential files.

Verification runs `nansen wallet export default --reveal`, which decrypts the wallet's private keys; the output goes to /dev/null, but the command still loads key material and the same pattern recurs on lines 141, 156, 186 and 220.
Wallet creation and re-secure commands (also line 194) pass a user-supplied wallet password inline as NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD=..., which exposes it to shell history and the process environment.

allowed-tools grants only Bash(nansen:*), but the instructions also run source, ls, rm -f, unset and shell conditionals, including deleting ~/.nansen/.env on line 123, which go beyond the declared tool scope.
The install block pulls the npm package nansen-cli (providing the nansen binary), so the skill installs third-party code from the npm registry.
The authentication paragraph describes a nansen:api browser-session login as an alternative to the API key and links to a github.com doc, while the only declared requirement is the nansen binary.
The inspect header shows Moderate CLEAN on line 13 but Security SUSPICIOUS with warnings on line 21, so the registry's own signals disagree.
The skill card admits the security assessment is incomplete because two local references were unresolved, and also notes the migration steps may not reliably complete (line 52).
